oracle: projects/xml/c/libxmlb/oracle.py (Python expat without namespace processing, ordered attributes)
output_name_form: raw qualified names (prefix:local); xmlns/xmlns:* are ordinary attributes
api: xb_builder_source_new(); xb_builder_source_load_xml(source, NUL-terminated copy of the local bytes, XB_BUILDER_SOURCE_FLAG_LITERAL_TEXT, &error); xb_builder_new(); xb_builder_import_source; xb_builder_compile(builder, XB_BUILDER_COMPILE_FLAG_NONE, NULL, &error); walk the XbSilo from xb_silo_get_root with xb_node_get_element, xb_node_attr_iter_init/next, xb_node_get_text, xb_node_get_child, xb_node_get_next and xb_node_get_tail
namespace_semantics: Neither libxmlb 0.3.30 nor GLib's GMarkup implements Namespaces in XML: element and attribute names are stored as written (prefix:local) and xmlns/xmlns:p are ordinary attributes in the silo. The adapter reports those names unchanged and resolves nothing.
coverage: LLVM source coverage of libxmlb and GLib, both built static and out of tree from their pinned releases; libxmlb's src/ is the parser subject and glib/gmarkup.c the underlying tokenizer
underlying_family: GLib GMarkup (g_markup_parse_context_parse), the XML-subset parser bundled in GLib
coverage_limit: Two valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE establish libxmlb's element, attribute, text and tail silo for them only, as a raw-name path: qualified names, xmlns attributes, attribute order and decoded values, depth and trimmed text runs. GMarkup tokenizes the markup and decodes the predefined entities, character references and CDATA (G_MARKUP_TREAT_CDATA_AS_TEXT); libxmlb builds and compiles the silo. Comments and processing instructions are not stored. GMarkup is documented as a subset parser (no DTDs, no external entities) and is not namespace-aware; no namespace URI, expanded name or in-scope binding is reported. xb_builder_source_load_xml takes a NUL-terminated string, so bytes after a NUL are not parsed. Other encodings, XML 1.1 and well-formedness rejection are not established. The expected outputs come from oracle.py (Python pyexpat in non-namespace mode, a different family from GMarkup).
